prerequisites: Sistemas de Control (Control Systems) or an equivalent course, covering classic control techniques, controller design using root locus, frequency domain design, and an introduction to state-space control.
Knowledge of Matlab/Simulink, especially the control toolbox.
Familiarity with Python, including libraries like numpy, matplotlib, pandas, and scikit-learn.

learning_outcomes.text: Interpret process state information from common graphical representations in industrial supervision systems.
Implement a supervision system in a SCADA system for monitoring an industrial process, with the ability to detect and diagnose simple faults.
Determine a dynamic process model suitable for control system design using empirical procedures.
Tune the parameters of the most important industrial PID controller formulations, using theoretical and empirical methods.
Design and implement industrial process control systems with specific characteristics such as dead times, typical nonlinearities, and coupled variables, among others.

syllabus_topics: Considerations for pole selection in assignment methods.
Optimal control. Symmetric root locus (SRL). LQR design.
Control of processes with dead times (Smith Predictor).
Principles of fault detection and identification. Analytical redundancy.
PCA techniques. PCA decomposition and calculation of projections. Contribution graphs, scores, etc.
Practical part: simulation exercises covering practical examples of state-space and PID control system design, as well as examples of feature extraction and classification for supervision.

assessment_methods.method: Theory exam (written test: problems, theoretical questions, multiple-choice, short answer, numerical exercises)
Practical exercises and/or presentation of work in the laboratory
Active participation (attendance, initiative, answering questions, active work on exercises)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum score of 4 out of 10 is required for the theory block. If this minimum is met, the final grade is calculated as 0.7 * Theory + 0.2 * Practices + 0.1 * Active Participation. If the minimum theory score is not met, the final grade will be the minimum of the calculated formula and 4.0. Formal aspects such as legibility and grammar are considered, and students may be asked to defend their work in case of doubts about authorship or unauthorized means. For extraordinary calls, the grading system is the same, but only the theoretical exam is conducted (70%), with the practice and participation scores (30%) carried over from the teaching period. For differentiated evaluation, students will take the theoretical exam (T) and a practical exam (P), with the same grading system and considerations, and an Active Participation (A) score of 0.
